chunks: Al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Abd al-Karim from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the divorced woman whose husband divorces her, and she does not know [of it] except after a year, and the woman whose husband dies, and she does not know of his death except after a year. He said: If two just witnesses come, then they do not observe the waiting period, and if not, they observe the waiting period.

key_terms.الْمَتَوَفَّى: The woman whose husband has died

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a woman who discovers her husband's divorce or death after a long delay?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's al-Istibsar clarifies the legal mechanism for determining the start of the waiting period (iddah) when a husband's death or divorce is delayed in reaching the wife. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that the iddah is calculated from the date of the event if two just witnesses testify to it, otherwise it begins from the date she receives news, reflecting the Shia emphasis on evidentiary proof in personal status law. This ruling ensures fairness by preventing women from being burdened with an indefinite or excessive waiting period due to lack of knowledge.
